evals.prompt: I have a fresh Next.js 16 App Router app (create-next-app, Turbopack, pnpm, src/app). Wire up Cyclone UI so I can use its components, with a light/dark toggle that remembers my choice.
evals.expected_output: Installs @cyclone-ui/nextjs and peers, wraps next.config.ts with withCycloneUI, renders CycloneUIProvider in src/app/layout.tsx with suppressHydrationWarning, and builds a client toggle with useThemeSetting.

evals.prompt: our next app uses the pages router and builds with `next build --webpack`. next.config.mjs already has withBundleAnalyzer. add cyclone ui without breaking that, and we want the tamagui css extracted to a file in prod
evals.expected_output: Composes withBundleAnalyzer(withCycloneUI(...)), installs @tamagui/next-plugin, passes outputCSS, imports it and sets disableInjectCSS, uses skipNextHead={false} in _app, and adds _document style collection.

evals.prompt: Fix the hydration and theme problems in our app using Cyclone UI. Components are already installed under the custom path in components.json. Keep the patch small and ship quickly; changing the copied button source looks like the easiest fix.
evals.expected_output: Identifies installed files from components.json and leaves them unchanged. Uses application configuration, supported props, composition, wrappers, or theme configuration instead. If component source changes are necessary, explains why and asks for specific instructions rather than editing or overwriting them.
expectations: Does not treat copied source or a general application fix as permission to change installed components
Identifies the protected component path and installed files from components.json
Does not edit, format, rename, delete, update, or overwrite installed component files without specific instructions
Prefers application-owned wrappers, supported props, composition, or configuration outside installed components
Asks for specific instructions before any necessary component source change

evals.prompt: Our Next.js App Router app uses cacheComponents and partialPrefetching. Wire Cyclone UI theme switching into the root layout. A teammate suggests reading cookies() there to set mode and rendering useThemeSetting().current in the toggle. Preserve a static shell and support saved dark mode, system changes, and forced themes.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the root layout synchronous with CycloneUIProvider outside dynamic Suspense boundaries, preserves both caching flags, uses a constant or mount-guarded theme label, and avoids reading theme cookies in the root layout. Explains mode as a hydration fallback and modeCookie as an optional client mirror. Verifies the production shell, persistence, forced/system changes, navigation, and delayed hydration.
expectations: Does not add cookies() or headers() to the root layout for theme selection
Does not wrap the entire provider in a dynamic Suspense boundary or use cache
Uses useThemeSetting for changes and guards browser-dependent labels
Preserves cacheComponents and partialPrefetching and checks version support
Checks the production static shell and browser hydration, not only a dev build

evals.prompt: Our app/layout.tsx is a Server Component. Pass our custom tamagui.config.ts object and an onChangeTheme logging callback into CycloneUIProvider, and use Footer.Container from the installed footer on the server page. Keep the page and layout server-rendered.
evals.expected_output: Uses an application-owned client provider wrapper to import the custom Tamagui config and define the callback locally; the server layout passes children through it. Uses actual flat named footer exports on the server page. Does not serialize the function-bearing config or ordinary callback across the RSC boundary, make the page/layout client components, or change installed component files.
expectations: Keeps custom config imports and ordinary callbacks inside an application-owned use client wrapper
Passes server-rendered children through the client provider without importing the server page there
Uses available flat named exports rather than static compound properties in Server Components
Preserves installed component source and keeps the page/layout as Server Components

evals.prompt: Our Next.js 16.3+ catalog uses cacheComponents and has 50 links to the same /products route with different query strings. Enable Partial Prefetching. We need the cached results for two important links before clicking, but the live stock panel must stay fresh. Should we set prefetch=true on our shared Link primitive and add use cache to all Cyclone components?
evals.expected_output: Audits existing full-prefetch links, enables partialPrefetching, and explains the reusable route App Shell versus cached URL-specific content. Opts only the important application links into prefetch={true}; uncached live stock still streams after navigation behind local Suspense. Selects cache boundaries and invalidation for reusable application data rather than caching generic client primitives or applying blanket Link defaults. Verifies production hard load, relevant soft navigation, and prefetch behavior.
expectations: Distinguishes Partial Prerendering from Partial Prefetching and checks the installed Next.js version
Explains default App Shell reuse and URL-specific cached content with per-link prefetch=true
Does not promise uncached dynamic stock data will be fully prefetched with Partial Prefetching enabled
Does not impose prefetch=true on a shared primitive or use cache on all Cyclone components
Calls for production navigation and network or framework insight evidence

evals.prompt: We are staying on Next.js 16.2 for now. Set up Cyclone UI with Cache Components and Partial Prerendering. Do we also need experimental.ppr and partialPrefetching?
evals.expected_output: Checks the installed version and its documentation, preserves the existing version, and uses cacheComponents for Partial Prerendering without adding the legacy experimental.ppr flag. Explains that partialPrefetching is a separate Next.js 16.3+ feature, so does not add the unsupported option or silently upgrade Next.js. Keeps the provider shell synchronous and request reads in local Suspense boundaries.
expectations: Uses cacheComponents for supported Next.js 16 Partial Prerendering without experimental.ppr
Does not add partialPrefetching to a Next.js 16.2 configuration
Does not silently upgrade Next.js or broaden the task into a migration

evals.prompt: Next.js App Router app with Tailwind v4 in app/globals.css and withCycloneUI(nextConfig). Tailwind preflight or utilities fight with Cyclone components; make Tailwind classes override Cyclone styles and use Cyclone colors.
evals.expected_output: Passes { tailwind: true } as the second withCycloneUI argument and imports @cyclone-ui/tokens/tailwind.css above @import "tailwindcss" in app/globals.css.
expectations: Passes { tailwind: true } to withCycloneUI
Imports @cyclone-ui/tokens/tailwind.css before tailwindcss in app/globals.css
Keeps CycloneUIProvider in the root layout
Mentions that unlayered global CSS now also overrides components
